title: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
old_text: Penalized a public servant knowingly disobeying any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself, intending to cause injury to any person, with simple imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely to cause injury to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or with fine, or with both (IPC Section 166).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 198).
explanation: Holds public servants criminally accountable for deliberate statutory disobedience calculated to cause injury to citizens. Renumbered from IPC Section 166.

title: Public servant disobeying direction under law
old_text: Penalized public servants knowingly disobeying legal directions prohibiting unlawful attendance requirements or failing to record FIRs in sexual offences with rigorous imprisonment from 6 months to 2 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of law prohibiting requiring attendance of any person at any place, or knowingly disobeys directions regulating investigation procedures, or fails to record any information given under cognizable offences (especially sexual offences), shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than six months up to two years, and fine.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 6 months up to 2 years, and fine (IPC Section 166A).
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to two years, and fine (BNS Section 199).
explanation: Strict compliance mandate for police officers penalizing refusal to register FIRs in sexual crimes or harassing vulnerable witnesses during investigations. Renumbered from IPC Section 166A.

title: Punishment for non-treatment of victim
old_text: Penalized persons in charge of public or private hospitals who failed to provide immediate free first-aid or medical treatment to rape or acid attack victims with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being in charge of any hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, State Government, local bodies or any other person, contravenes the provisions of law requiring immediate first-aid or medical treatment free of cost to victims of sexual assault or acid attacks, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both (IPC Section 166B).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one year, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 200).
explanation: Mandates immediate free emergency medical treatment for rape and acid attack victims across all private and government hospitals, penalizing hospital non-compliance. Renumbered from IPC Section 166B.

title: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury
old_text: Penalized public servants framing, preparing or translating documents incorrectly with intent to cause injury with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant charged with the preparation or translation of any document or electronic record, frames, prepares or translates that document or record in a manner which he knows or believes to be incorrect, with intent or knowledge that it will cause injury, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 167).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 201).
explanation: Penalizes falsification or manipulative translation of official government documents or electronic records by civil servants to cause citizen detriment. Renumbered from IPC Section 167.

title: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade
old_text: Penalized public servants legally bound not to engage in trade who unlawfully engaged in trade with simple imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant not to engage in trade, engages in trade, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both (IPC Section 168).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 202).
explanation: Prevents conflict of interest by penalizing government servants who operate private commercial businesses in violation of service conditions. Renumbered from IPC Section 168.

title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
old_text: Penalized public servants unlawfully bidding for or purchasing property with simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both, and property confiscated.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound not to purchase or bid for certain property, purchases or bids for that property, either in his own name or in the name of another, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both, and the property shall be confiscated.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, and property confiscated (IPC Section 169).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both, and property confiscated (BNS Section 203).
explanation: Prohibits public officials from purchasing or bidding for state-auctioned or distressed property under their official control, mandating forfeiture of purchased assets. Renumbered from IPC Section 169.

title: Personating a public servant
old_text: Penalized pretending to hold an office as a public servant and doing an act under colour of such office with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant, knowing that he does not hold such office, or falsely personates any other person holding such office, and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 170).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 204).
explanation: Penalizes impersonating police, tax, or administrative officers and attempting to exercise official authority. Renumbered from IPC Section 170.

title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent
old_text: Penalized wearing garb or carrying tokens resembling those of a public servant with fraudulent intent with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹200, or both.
new_text: Whoever, not belonging to a certain class of public servants, wears any garb or carries any token resembling that used by that class, with the intention that it may be believed that he belongs to that class, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹200, or both (IPC Section 171).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 205).
explanation: Penalizes civilians sporting official police, military, or civil badges, caps, or uniforms to deceive the public, increasing the maximum fine twenty-five-fold from ₹200 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 171.
